persons.name: Bennet Bailey
persons.note: INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED RESIDENT. Originally documented in Chicago post-office evidence; independent resident research now corroborates the identity. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Bailey, Bennet' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — dated 1835-05-20. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1). OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — A DATE OF DEATH, AND NOTHING ABOUT 1835. John Wentworth's roll of old settlers who had died since 1 January 1881, kept for the Calumet Club and printed in the Chicago Tribune of 25 April 1882, carries “Bennett Bailey, Nov.11. 1881.”. That corroborates a Chicago residence before 1840 and fixes the END of this life, which this record did not carry; it is not an arrival and it places nobody in the town on 1 July 1835. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer; the forename is bridged — the same forename with the final consonant doubled: the papers' post-office return prints 'Bailey, Bennet' and Wentworth's roll prints 'Bennett Bailey' (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). OLD SETTLERS, 1879 — A DATE THIS MAN GAVE FOR HIMSELF, AND STILL NOT A FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's FIRST reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, 27 May 1879, printed its register in the proceedings (Early Chicago, Chicago, 1879, pages 84-90), and this man's entry reads “Bailey, Bennet, | 1834, August, | Harford Co., Md. | 68 | Chicago.” — name, his own date of arrival, his birthplace, his age and his 1879 post-office address, in the register's five columns. The date of arrival is HIS RECOLLECTION, set down forty to sixty years after the event; the address is where he lived in 1879 and is never read as an 1835 residence. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Bennett Bailey,” (f1839_v0003, printed page 41, ward 1, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Bailey' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins B. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

residents.why: boarding in the division's least crowded dwelling

persons.name: R. Stewart
persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'R. stewart' and 'RK, STEW ART' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the American of 13 June 1835, column 3; the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 32; the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 7; the Democrat of 16 July 1834, column 7. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `attorney` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Royal Stewart,” (f1839_v0111, printed page 42, ward 1, voting for John H. Kinzie). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Stewart' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins R. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 7 times, as “STEWART ROYAL”, 1836-06-20 to 6/22/1836: 7 lots in the platted town — lot 1 of block 35 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L1BL35CHIOT, as printed); lot 1 of block 9 in the town the register codes CHIOTVO (L1BL9CHIOTVO, as printed); lot 2 of block 8 in the town the register codes CHIOTVO (L2BL8CHIOTVO, as printed); lot 2 of block 9 in the town the register codes CHIOTVO (L2BL9CHIOTVO, as printed); lot 3 of block 2 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L3BL2CHIOT, as printed); lot 3 of block 38 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L3BL38CHIOT, as printed); lot 7 of block 37 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L7BL37CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $47560.00 (ls1470, ls1471, ls1472, ls1473, ls1474, ls1475, ls1476). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $47560.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: STEWART ROYAL matches R. Stewart: the forename names R. Stewart of the 2 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name R. Stewart as a attorney at Chicago 4 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.

persons.name: Ezekiel Turner
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Ezekiel Turner' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 33, reprinted over 3 consecutive issues — dated 1834-07-02 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

citations.citation: The baptismal register of St Mary's, Chicago — the first Catholic parish in the town — opened by Father John Mary Irenaeus St. Cyr on 22 May 1833 and read here for the years 1833, 1834 and 1835: 57 entries in French and English naming children, parents, godparents and witnesses, with the priest's own signature under every one and eight autographs of the town's own people beside them.

transcribes.work: The baptismal register kept at Chicago by Father J. M. I. St. Cyr from May 1833
transcribes.note: THE ORIGINAL, and these eleven images are photographs of it. A reading made off them is scan_verified — the higher of this project's two reading grades — and it outranks the marriage and death pages of st_cyr_register_ichr_v4, which reached this project through a 1921-22 article and a web transcription.

what_it_supplies: 57 dated baptisms of 1833-1835 and 267 named readings of people — 46 of the entries at Chicago and 166 of the readings adults there
KINSHIP, which no other source this project holds gives at all: a child, its two parents and its two godparents on one dated line, 44 times over
the town's Catholic population — French, Métis, Irish and German — of whom 85 distinct adults reach no surname in the residents layer

eight AUTOGRAPHS: Mark Beaubien, Josette Laframboise, Augustin Bonné, Monique Nadeau, Jean Baptiste Lavigne, J. B. Beaubien, Robert A. Kinzie and Gwinthlean Whistler signing under the priest, each placing a named person at a named place on a named day in their own hand
two adult baptisms with AGES — Josette Laframboise Beaubien at 38 in June 1834 and Geneviève Medera at about 20 in June 1835 — which are the only ages this project has for either woman
the parish's own start date, 22 May 1833, on a page the book heads '1er Page'
the register's own arithmetic: pencil tallies of 19, 24 and 14 baptisms for 1833, 1834 and 1835, which check any reading of it
a hue and cry on the title page describing what a young man of the Illinois country wore in 1833 or 1834 — a white pea coat, gray pants and a fur cap
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, lot, street, dwelling or workplace — the register places nobody anywhere in the town, and names no church building on any of the eleven pages
residence, and this is the trap. A baptism documents a person at a font on a day. Presence is not residence and nothing here mints or regrades a resident
presence on 1 July 1835 for anyone not baptised or standing as sponsor within days of it
occupation. One entry writes 'Doctor Egan' — a title inside a name — and that is the only trade the book ever states

ALL CHICAGO. Entries 1-11 of 1834 were written at Bear Creek, the South Fork of the Sangamon and Springfield, in Sangamon County, on the priest's journey back from St. Louis. A reader who takes the book as a Chicago roll plants eleven households in the wrong county
reliable spelling. A French priest wrote Irish, English and German names and phoneticised Potawatomi and Odawa ones; the same woman is Nadeau, Nodeau and Nodou in his own hand on three pages
the sponsors of 1834 entry 4, which stood on a line the scan's frame cuts off
anything about 1836 or later. The two page-sides in the deposit that carry 1837-38 and 1849 entries are declared and not transcribed
